mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1 standard deviation from their respective 12-month means indicates a shift from construction to manufacturing activity, which historically precedes a mild positive equity risk premium and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: transition from housing to manufacturing cycle
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between the described INDPRO/HOUST regime and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months, combined with a flat federal funds rate, signals a risk of deflation, which historically increases the real value of debt and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for 2 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS stable (change < 0.1pp)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during episodes of CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months with stable FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between PAYEMS > 200k for three months and S&P 500 20-day returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) by more than one standard deviation from their 12-month means signals a precautionary savings regime, which historically precedes equity market weakness over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between the RSAFS/GDPC1 regime and S&P 500 60-day returns in out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive monthly INDPRO declines.
